aspects.says: A case is a request template whose unique fields are generated per run, graded field by field; a replayed message repeats its STAN and time and meets the host's duplicate check.
basis: section:10.3. A Case Is a Request Template and Every Field Its Answer Must Carry

aspects.says: Host certification proves one link against one network's specification; an EMV kernel approval, a PCI assessment or another network's certification does not cover it.
basis: section:10.1. Certification Proves One Host Link Against One Network's Specification

aspects.says: The network certified bytes, so a change of library, packager definition or channel after certification is cleared with the network before it goes live.
basis: section:10.6. The Certified Build Is the One That Goes Live

aspects.says: The log shows the message as the program built it and the packager may change it on the way out, so the evidence is a text hex dump of the bytes, found by STAN.
basis: section:10.5. The Evidence Is the Bytes That Left, Kept as Text and Found by STAN

aspects.says: A number with a correct check digit under a network's prefix may belong to a cardholder, since every printed card passes the check.
basis: section:10.4. A Test Card Is Issued for Testing, and the Luhn Check Only Says It Is Well Formed

aspects.says: The whole script runs against your own simulator on every build before the first test-host session, because sessions are scarce and a bug found in one costs another.
basis: section:10.2. Your Own Suite Runs Every Case Before the Test Host Sees One
aspects.reason: a planning habit with no behaviour of its own to run offline; units c10, c16 and s11 grade the jPOS harnesses that carry it out

aspects.says: Only cards issued for testing go to a test host; the Luhn check digit only catches typing errors, and a real card number in a log puts every copy under PCI DSS.
basis: section:10.4. A Test Card Is Issued for Testing, and the Luhn Check Only Says It Is Well Formed
